text: I have a sister, a widow, from whom I have been separated for a long time, and to whom I am almost everything. I shouldn’t like to say to her that I must leave her. She rather depends upon me, you see.” “Ah, that’s very proper; family feeling is very proper,” said Dr. Sloper. “I often think there is not enough of it in our city. I think I have heard of your sister.” “It is possible, but I rather doubt it; she lives so very quietly.” “As quietly, you mean,” the Doctor went on, with a short laugh, “as a lady may do who has several young children.” “Ah, my little nephews and nieces—that’s the very point!
